title: Fabian Hurzeler feels ‘no pressure’ from Brighton & Hove Albion hierarchy despite team’s flailing form
content:
Head coach Fabian Hurzeler says he feels only support, not pressure, from the bosses at Brighton & Hove Albion.

Hurzeler’s side have dropped from fifth in the Premier League table at the end of November to 14th, seven points above the relegation zone, after one win in 13 games.

Some supporters want Hurzeler to be sacked because of the downturn, which has turned the focus on the job security of the 32-year-old German coach.

“I feel no pressure,” said Hurzeler when asked if he feels under pressure from anyone at the top of the club during his press conference for Saturday night’s FA Cup fourth round tie away to Liverpool.

“I feel the pressure I put on myself to prepare the team the best I can, to be there for them and to improve them every day. That’s the most pressure I feel, because I always want to be the best version of myself, to try to be there for the club, try to be there for the fans, for the team, for the staff. And that’s the pressure I put on myself, that’s the biggest pressure I can have.

“I really feel the support from the club, we have daily exchanges. We speak quite honestly with each other. We talk about the reality of where we are at the moment. The reality is that it’s not an easy situation, but in these tough times, you really see how you act with each other, how you treat each other, how you support each other.

“I really feel supported. I really feel the belief from the club and now it’s about me, it’s about us to give something back.”

Wednesday’s 1-0 defeat at Aston Villa leaves Brighton with two points out of a possible 15 since drawing 1-1 at Manchester City and winning 2-1 at Manchester United in the third round of the FA Cup in January.

“On the one side, it’s very important to focus on performances and to focus on the things you can control. On the other side, we all know this game is a game of results, especially for me as a head coach,” Hurzeler said. “We need a result. The club and all the supporters there (at Villa) were waiting for this one result. We all keep fighting for this.

“We try to commit to this and we are all convinced that if we keep doing the things we did, if we keep having these performances we had, then we are all convinced that we will get the results we all need and deserve, especially our fans deserve it because their support (at Villa) was incredible.

“For 90 minutes they were there for us. They helped us. They pushed us and they can definitely be frustrated about the recent results. But, they were amazing and therefore I was very thankful and hope that we can give them something back on Saturday.”

Hurzeler’s selection options for the trip to Anfield are increased by the return of Mats Wieffer from a toe injury which ruled the Dutch midfielder turned right-back out of the first eight matches of the calendar year.

Brighton have been staying at the national football centre at St George’s Park since the Villa game to prepare for the visit to Anfield, where they lost 2-0 in the league in December.
